records.issue_text: [BUG] The `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction is registered only in the discover dataset, but `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` gates the transformation on `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returning True unconditionally for the errors dataset, so queries routed to the errors dataset receive the column `upsampled_count() as count` that no function registry knows and fail to resolve. Any request hitting organization_events_stats with the errors dataset over an all-allowlisted org gets a 500/invalid-function Snuba error instead of stats; the tests never exercise the errors dataset (all test URLs use the default discover dataset), so this path is entirely unverified.
records.rationale: The diff adds the SnQL function `upsampled_count` only to the discover dataset (`src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py`), but the new gating logic explicitly enables the transformation for the errors dataset: `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns `True` when `dataset == errors` (`src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`). When enabled, `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` rewrites `count()` to `"upsampled_count() as count"`, and `organization_events_stats.py` then passes these transformed columns to the query (`y_axes` / `selected_columns`). records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff adds a git submodule `sentry-repo` pointing at an external commit, meaning the actual ingestion-side piece that populates `sample_weight` lives outside this repository, and the only in-repo writer is a test factory (`_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling`). Main-repo deployments without the exact submodule commit registered query `sum(sample_weight)` against an events table where nothing populates the column, so allowlisted projects get counts of 0/null instead of upsampled counts; the helper module's assumption "schema ensures sample_weight exists" is unverifiable and unenforced in this codebase.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The upsampled_count SnQL function reads a sample_weight column that no writer anywhere in this diff (or the event ingestion path it touches) produces — the only new writer is the test-only factory hook _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling, which sets sample_rate, not sample_weight. The feature ships inert-to-corrupting: even new events ingested after deploy carry no sample_weight (the normalization change in factories.py only affects test event storage and writes a differently-named field), so sum(sample_weight) is NULL/0 for 100% of rows and the upsampled count understates real error volume by the full amount rather than upsampling it. No dual-write exists between the old count() representation and the new sample_weight representation, so any later backfill/cutover will find nothing to migrate from.
